saints.name: St. Francis Caracciolo
saints.title: Priest and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: An Italian nobleman who founded a religious order devoted above all to the Blessed Sacrament…
biography: Born Ascanio Caracciolo at Villa Santa Maria in the Abruzzi in 1563, he was cured of a sickness thought mortal after vowing his life to God, and went to Naples to study for the priesthood, where he took the name Francis in a confraternity serving condemned prisoners. A letter of John Augustine Adorno, delivered to him by mistake, he read as God's call to found a new order.

The Clerics Regular Minor, approved by Pope Sixtus V in 1588, added to the three usual vows a fourth: never to seek any dignity or office. Their life joined works of charity with perpetual adoration of the Blessed Sacrament day and night. Superior general from 1593, after Adorno's death, Francis begged in the streets for the poor, spent hours before the tabernacle, and refused a bishopric from Pope Paul V.

In 1608 he went to Agnone to open a new house, pausing to pray the night at the Holy House of Loreto, and died there of a fever on 4 June. Canonized by Pope Pius VII in 1807, he rests at Naples, which chose him in 1838 as one of her patrons.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Clerks Regular Minor and Eucharistic devotion.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
